mainTopic: Whether avoiding טומאת מת counts as a painful vow, and a new משנה about a woman's vow not to benefit from people: is her husband one of the 'people'?
overview: This daf first finishes a discussion about a נזירה whose husband nullified her vow. The גמרא asks whether he could really have nullified only the painful wine part and not the טומאת מת part, since the ברייתא frees her from the offerings of an impure נזיר. It answers that avoiding the dead is also painful, because רבי מאיר teaches that whoever eulogizes, weeps for and buries others will receive the same. Then a new משנה begins. A woman who vows not to benefit from people cannot have the vow nullified by her husband, but she may still take לקט, שכחה and פאה. A vow forbidding כהנים and לוים in general does not stop them from taking their gifts. A vow against specific ones sends the gifts to others. The גמרא then asks whether a husband counts as one of the 'people' in her vow. עולא, רבא and רב נחמן each answer differently.

steps.title: Maybe the husband only nullified the wine part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: could the husband have nullified only the painful wine part of her נזירות and not the seemingly painless טומאת מת part? The ברייתא implies the whole vow fell away, which challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the husband nullified the wine part, because giving up wine causes her pain, but he did not nullify the טומאת מת part, because staying away from the dead causes her no pain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty from the ברייתא. If the husband could only nullify the painful wine part, why does the ברייתא free her from the offerings for becoming impure from the dead? The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can nullify vows that cause his wife pain (עינוי נפש). Giving up wine clearly hurts, but avoiding contact with the dead seems to cost her nothing. Yet the ברייתא frees her from the טומאה offerings, so it seems the nullification reached even the painless part. That would make it a difficulty for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He nullified (the husband canceling his wife's vow)
Impurity that comes from contact with a dead body

phrases.english: Perhaps from wine, which causes her pain —
phrases.notes: This is about a woman who took on נזירות, which forbids both wine and becoming impure from the dead.

phrases.english: he nullified for her,
but from impurity of the dead, which causes her no pain —
he did not nullify for her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי יוחנן's view, bringing the ברייתא of the נזירה whose husband nullified her vow as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position, challenged from the ברייתא where the nullification frees her even from the טומאת מת offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Avoiding the dead seems painless, so the husband should only be able to nullify the wine part. Yet the ברייתא exempts her from the טומאה offerings, which implies the painless part was nullified too.

steps.title: Avoiding the dead is also painful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a vow to avoid טומאת מת is also painful. She cannot honor the dead, and רבי מאיר teaches that one who honors others at their death will be honored in turn.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: avoiding טומאת מת also causes her pain, as the פסוק says, 'And the living shall lay it to his heart.' רבי מאיר taught that this means: whoever eulogizes others will be eulogized, whoever weeps for others will be wept for, and whoever buries others will be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that staying away from the dead really is painful for her, so both parts of the vow count as pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she cannot become impure from the dead, she cannot eulogize, mourn at, or bury others. רבי מאיר reads the פסוק as teaching that how you treat others at their death is how you will be treated at yours. The thought that she may not be properly mourned is real distress, so this part of the vow also counts as a vow of pain.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow to avoid טומאת מת counts as a vow of pain (עינוי נפש), because it keeps her from honoring the dead, and רבי מאיר teaches that one who honors the dead is honored in return.

phrases.english: They say: from impurity of the dead also
she has pain —
as it is written: "And the living shall lay it to his heart,"
and it was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
What is meant by "And the living shall lay it to his heart"?
One who eulogizes will be eulogized,
one who weeps will be wept for,
one who buries will be buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מִטּוּמְאַת מֵת נָמֵי אִית לַהּ צַעֲרָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption that avoiding טומאת מת causes no pain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Avoiding the dead costs her nothing, so the husband could not nullify that part of the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Avoiding the dead stops her from honoring others at their death, which is real distress. So this part of the vow is also a vow of pain, and the ברייתא is no difficulty for רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A vow not to benefit from people
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if a woman vows not to benefit from people, her husband cannot nullify the vow, but she may still take לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman said, 'Benefit from people is קונם for me,' her husband cannot nullify the vow. She may still benefit from לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a woman who forbids herself from benefiting from other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even under this vow, she may still take the gifts the תורה leaves for the poor: לקט, שכחה and פאה. The משנה rules that her husband cannot nullify this vow, and it places that ruling right next to the fact that she still has these gifts. The גמרא will explain the reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (a new משנה begins here)
A word used to make something forbidden like a קרבן
Gifts the תורה leaves for the poor: fallen stalks, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"It is konam that I benefit from people" —
he cannot nullify it,
and she may benefit
from gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her husband cannot nullify a vow not to benefit from people, and she may still take לקט, שכחה and פאה.

steps.title: Forbidding all כהנים and לוים from benefiting
steps.stepSummary: If a person forbids כהנים and לוים in general from benefiting from him, they take their gifts from him against his will.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'כהנים and לוים benefiting from me is קונם,' they take their gifts against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a man who tries to keep all כהנים and לוים from benefiting from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts such as תרומה and מעשר are owed to כהנים and לוים as a group. His vow cannot cancel that obligation, so they take the gifts even though he objects.

phrases.english: "It is konam that priests and Levites benefit from me" —
they take against his will.
phrases.notes: They take the gifts the תורה gives them, like תרומה and מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow forbidding all כהנים and לוים does not stop them from taking their gifts.

steps.title: Forbidding specific כהנים and לוים
steps.stepSummary: If he forbids only certain named כהנים and לוים, other כהנים and לוים take the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'These כהנים and these לוים may not benefit from me,' other כהנים and לוים take the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the general vow with a vow that names specific כהנים and לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here his vow is limited to particular people. The gifts can still reach כהנים and לוים, just not these ones, so other כהנים and לוים receive them. This differs from step 4, where he forbade כהנים and לוים in general, and they could take the gifts against his will.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. When he forbids כהנים and לוים in general, they take the gifts anyway. When he names specific ones, those specific people don't take, but others do.
steps.whatToRemember: A general vow cannot block the gifts owed to כהנים and לוים. A vow naming specific ones only sends the gifts to other כהנים and לוים.

phrases.english: "These priests and these Levites benefiting from me [is konam]" —
phrases.notes: The word קונם isn't actually said here; the גמרא carries it over from the case before.

phrases.english: others take.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 4: a vow against specific people instead of the whole group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he names specific כהנים and לוים, the gifts go to other כהנים and לוים.

steps.title: Inference from the first clause: the husband is not part of 'people'
steps.stepSummary: From the rule that the husband cannot nullify the vow, the גמרא infers that she can still eat from his food, so a husband is not included in ״בריות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: It seems she can still be fed from her husband's things. This shows that a husband is not counted as part of 'people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the first part of the משנה. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why can't the husband nullify her vow? The simple answer is that it doesn't hurt her much, because she can still eat his food. That only works if her vow about 'people' does not include her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
By inference; we learn it from what was said
People / creatures; the word she used in her vow

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Apparently, it is possible for her to be fed from his,
phrases.notes: 'His' means her husband's food and property. That is why the husband can't nullify: she isn't really suffering.

phrases.english: which proves by inference that a husband
is not included in 'people.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the first clause, the husband is not included in ״בריות״, so she may still be supported by him.

steps.title: The later clause implies the husband is part of 'people'
steps.stepSummary: The later clause lists only לקט, שכחה and פאה as allowed, which implies she may not eat from her husband. So he is included in ״בריות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the later clause: she may benefit from gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field. But from her husband she may not eat! This shows a husband IS included in 'people'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 6 by pointing to the next words of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she could eat her husband's food, why would the משנה need to tell us she can take poor people's gifts? Mentioning only those gifts suggests she can't benefit from her husband. So the two parts of the משנה seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause; look at the end of the משנה

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
she may benefit
from gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field,
but from the husband's she may not eat,
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't say this outright. The גמרא reads it into the משנה, since only the poor-gifts are mentioned.

phrases.english: apparently a husband is included in 'people'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the inference of step 6 using the very next clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a husband is not included in ״בריות״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא lists only the poor-gifts as allowed, which implies the husband's food is forbidden, so the רישא and סיפא contradict.

steps.title: עולא: husband not included; the משנה gives two reasons
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the husband is not included in ״בריות״. The משנה gives two reasons he can't nullify: she can eat his food, and also she can take לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Really, the husband is not included in 'people.' And there is another reason he cannot nullify: because she can benefit from gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the contradiction by keeping step 6 as true and reading the later clause as an extra reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor-gifts clause doesn't mean the husband's food is forbidden. It just adds a second reason the vow isn't painful enough to nullify. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; keeps the original position

phrases.english: עולא said:
Actually, he is not included in 'people,'
and furthermore: he cannot nullify —
because she may benefit
from gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא לְעוֹלָם לָאו בִּכְלַל בְּרִיּוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 while keeping the inference of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the סיפא as an extra reason, not as a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא implies the husband's food is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband is not included. The סיפא just adds a second reason he can't nullify.

steps.title: רבא: husband is included; the משנה is explaining its reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the husband is included in ״בריות״. The סיפא explains why he can't nullify: she can still take לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, the husband is included in 'people.' The משנה is saying 'what is the reason': Why can't he nullify? Because she can benefit from gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the other way: he keeps the later clause and drops the inference from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, she really may not benefit from her husband. He still can't nullify, and the only reason is that the poor-gifts keep her from real suffering. The first clause never meant she can eat his food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is saying 'what is the reason'; the second part explains the first

steps.confusionAlert: רבא disagrees with עולא. עולא says the husband is NOT included; רבא says he IS included.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Actually, a husband is included in 'people,'
and it is saying 'what is the reason':
phrases.notes: Read the משנה as a question and answer: the second half explains the first half.

phrases.english: What is the reason he cannot nullify?
Because she may benefit
from gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר לְעוֹלָם בַּעַל בִּכְלַל בְּרִיּוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to step 7, opposite to עולא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference from the רישא and reads the סיפא as the reason for it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא implies she can eat her husband's food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband is included. The only reason he can't nullify is the poor-gifts.

steps.title: רב נחמן: husband not included; the later clause is about after divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the husband is not included in ״בריות״. The סיפא teaches that if she is divorced, she can still take לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Really, the husband is not included in 'people.' And this is what the משנה teaches: if she gets divorced, she can still benefit from gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a third answer: the two clauses describe two different times, during marriage and after divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While married, she can eat her husband's food, so he can't nullify. Once divorced, he becomes like any other person and is forbidden to her. Even then she is not stuck, because she can take the poor-gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches; explains the משנה's meaning

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers: עולא says the husband is not included and the משנה gives two reasons. רבא says the husband is included and the poor-gifts are the only reason. רב נחמן says the husband is not included and the poor-gifts clause is about after a divorce.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
Actually, a husband is not included in 'people.'
And this is what it teaches:
if she became divorced, she may benefit
from gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר לְעוֹלָם בַּעַל לָאו בִּכְלַל בְּרִיּוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 7, agreeing with עולא that the husband is not included but explaining the סיפא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the סיפא in a different case (after divorce)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is about while she is married, so it implies the husband's food is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband is not included while married. The סיפא is about after divorce, when she can still take the poor-gifts.
